We have carbon NMR data with chemical shifts. Need to determine number of carbonyl (C=O) groups. Carbonyl carbons typically appear around 160-220 ppm (for ketones, aldehydes, esters, acids). The provided shifts are all between 124.85 and 62.10, etc. No high ppm signals. So likely zero carbonyl groups.

But could be conjugated carbonyls maybe around 190-200, not present. So answer 0.

Check if any other data needed? Could also use IR to see C=O stretch ~1700 cm-1. Could request IR to confirm, but carbon NMR already suggests none. To be safe, maybe get IR. But cost minimal. Let's get IR.
